segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making time, Dana. I wanted to confirm the scope we discussed for the calibration tracking rollout: 42 technician seats, 6 supervisor seats, and the asset import for roughly 3,800 gauges and meters at the Dayton site.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That matches. We may add the Toledo lab later, but not before Q3. For Dayton, the big thing is being live by April 15 because our audit window opens May 6.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Understood. The implementation plan has a March 18 kickoff, two data review sessions, and user training the week of April 8. That gives you about two weeks of cushion before the audit.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. On pricing, the finance team asked if the annual total is still $58,400, including the import work.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes. That is $49,200 for the subscription and $9,200 for one-time services. The pricing sheet is approved for those numbers through February 29, and it includes standard support.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Good. Our billing preference is one invoice upfront, net 30. Can you list the PO number on it? It’ll be PO-7716.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep, we can put PO-7716 on the invoice. The order form will show net 30, one annual invoice, service start date March 18, and initial term through March 17 next year.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Contract terms are fine if the data security exhibit is the one you sent last week. Legal had no edits to that version.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Great, same exhibit, no changes. I’ll send the final order form today for e-signature, and once it’s signed you’ll get the kickoff invite with the project lead copied.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Perfect. Send it to me and copy Martin in procurement. If we can sign by Friday, I think we’re in good shape.
